newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weak in jittery market.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weak in jittery market.

text.p: * Central Bank sells $56.5 million at 26.24 pesos

Jitters caused by uncertainty over the dollar requirements of oil companies and the closing out of peso positions by interest rate arbitrageurs pulled down the Philippine peso, traders said on Monday.
The peso ended at its day-low of 26.24 pesos to the dollar from the previous close of 26.235. The day's average was 26.238 versus 26.231.

"The peso positions of the arbitrageurs just matured. They bought dollars and parked them in the forex deposits. They're just waiting for the right levels in peso interest rates before coming in," said a dealer.
Banks were also anticipating higher demand from oil companies who have indicated they may need $39 million this week.

The situation got worse when the Central Bank raised its bid rate to 26.234 from 26.22 pesos but kept its offer rate at 26.24 pesos, traders said. "It just encouraged more buying of dollars," said one.
The Central Bank unloaded a total of $56.5 million.
